dossier.purpose: Nosey Parker (`noseyparker`) is a Rust command-line secret scanner from Praetorian. `scan` walks files, directories, local Git repositories (all blobs in the object database), HTTPS Git URLs, GitHub users/orgs, and JSONL-streamed content. It matches them against 183 YAML-defined regex rules (Vectorscan prefilter plus Rust regex captures), groups matches into deduplicated findings stored in a local SQLite 'datastore', and `report`/`summarize` emit human, JSON, JSONL or (experimental) SARIF output. Per the code: it does not verify whether found credentials are live, it has no staged-changes/pre-commit mode, and it exits 0 whether or not findings exist.

claims.claim: Nosey Parker is a CLI tool that finds secrets and sensitive information in textual data; essentially a special-purpose grep-like tool for detection of secrets.
Designed for offensive security (e.g., red-team lateral movement) but can also be useful for defensive security testing; has found secrets in hundreds of offensive security engagements at Praetorian.
Natively scans files, directories, GitHub, and Git history, and has an extensible input enumeration mechanism.
Uses regular expressions with 183 patterns chosen for high precision based on feedback from security engineers.
Deduplicates matches that share the same secret, reducing review burden by 10-1000x or more.
Can scan at GB/s on a multicore system and has scanned inputs as large as 20TB during security engagements.
Typical workflow is three phases: scan inputs, report details, review and triage findings; interactive review/annotation is via the separate companion project Nosey Parker Explorer.

Install options: Homebrew formula, prebuilt x86_64/aarch64 Linux and macOS binaries on the latest release page, Docker images (Debian and Alpine base, x86_64/aarch64) on ghcr.io, Arch Linux AUR package, or build from source.
Does not build natively on Windows (#121); it is possible to run on Windows using WSL1 and the native Linux release.
Source builds tested on several Ubuntu versions and macOS on x86_64 and aarch64; build needs cargo, cmake, boost >=1.57, git, patch, pkg-config, sha256sum, zsh.

Can scan a Git repo from an HTTPS URL and the repos of a GitHub user or organization; an optional GitHub token in NP_GITHUB_TOKEN gives a higher API rate limit and may make additional repositories accessible.
Reports findings in human-readable and JSON formats; additional output formats including JSON and JSON lines are available via --format.
Third-party integrations: Homebrew and Arch packages, a GitHub Action (bpsizemore/noseyparker-action), a DefectDojo parser for Nosey Parker v0.16 JSON, and Nemesis support.
The project has pre-commit hooks that contributors are encouraged to install via `pre-commit install`.

Environment variables read: NP_DATASTORE, NP_GITHUB_TOKEN, NP_LOG, NO_COLOR (args.rs:181, 594-646; main.rs:45-50).

integrations.sdk_or_api: No SDK or HTTP API. Workspace crates are `publish = false` (Cargo.toml:17) and the changelog calls the Rust crate APIs an implementation detail (CHANGELOG.md:7). Machine-readable interfaces: `report`/`summarize` JSON and JSONL, experimental SARIF (args.rs:1287-1327), a JSON Schema of the report JSON via `generate json-schema` (args.rs:1210-1211), and JSONL input via `scan --enumerator` (args.rs:894-912). integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found - grep for claude/codex/copilot/cursor/agent skill across the repo returns nothing. The only AI-vendor material is detection rules for AI-provider API keys (e.g., crates/noseyparker/data/default/builtin/rules/anthropic.yml:3-12, matching sk-ant-api keys), which are scanning rules, not an integration.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics, crash-reporting, update-check or phone-home code found: grep over crates/, docs/, scripts/ and workflows for telemetry/analytics/sentry/usage-stats/update-check terms finds nothing relevant, Cargo.lock lists no telemetry/analytics crates (only the reqwest/hyper/openssl HTTP stack, Cargo.lock:3745), and the README is silent on telemetry. No account or registration is required; a GitHub token is optional. Network use is limited to: (1) `git clone --bare|--mirror` and `git remote update --prune` run through the system `git` binary for --git-url and --github-* inputs, with global/system git config disabled (crates/noseyparker-cli/src/cmd_scan.rs:1174-1263; crates/noseyparker/src/git_binary.rs:48-109); only https URLs without embedded credentials, query or fragment are accepted (crates/noseyparker/src/git_url.rs:41-92). (2) Read-only GET requests to the GitHub REST API (default https://api.github.com/, or a GitHub Enterprise URL via --github-api-url) to list repos: rate_limit, users/{u}, users/{u}/repos, orgs/{o}/repos, orgs/{o}/members, organizations (crates/noseyparker/src/github/client.rs:35-68, 254-267; github.rs:47-62), User-Agent `noseyparker` (client_builder.rs:17). NP_GITHUB_TOKEN is read only from the environment, held as a secrecy::SecretString and sent as a bearer token (client_builder.rs:46-68; auth.rs:12; client.rs:261-264); the same variable is handed to git through an always-configured inline credential helper that echoes $NP_GITHUB_TOKEN (git_binary.rs:30-36), and GitUrl allows any HTTPS host (git_url.rs:59-61), so the token may be offered to non-GitHub hosts that request credentials (code-reading inference, not tested). (3) Scanning local files, directories, local repos and --enumerator files uses no network. (4) --ignore-certs disables TLS verification for both git (GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY) and the API client (args.rs:339-341; git_binary.rs:53-55; client_builder.rs:72-75). Findings are never transmitted; they are written to a local SQLite datastore (datastore.rs:1034-1051). The binary embeds build-host metadata (OS, CPU, rustc, git SHA) shown by --version (crates/noseyparker-cli/build.rs:8-15; args.rs:38-71); this is local only. The test suite and CI call the live GitHub API and clone GitHub repos (crates/noseyparker-cli/tests/github/mod.rs; tests/scan/appmaker/mod.rs:18-34; ci.yml:173-180).

entry_points.what: Binary main(): parses args, sets up logging/rlimits, dispatches to subcommands, exits 2 only on error (main.rs:100-136). Cargo's bin name is `noseyparker-cli`; scripts/create-release.zsh:119 renames it to `noseyparker`.
clap definition of every command and option, including input specifiers, rule selection, report filters/formats, env-var bindings.
`scan` pipeline: load rules, clone/update Git URLs, enumerate inputs, parallel scan, batched SQLite writes, summary print.
`report` command (human/json/jsonl in this file; cmd_report/human_format.rs and cmd_report/sarif_format.rs for the other formats).
`summarize` command: per-rule counts as human table, JSON or JSONL.
`rules check` linter: unique/well-formed IDs, ruleset resolution, every rule in some ruleset, examples/negative_examples assertions; nonzero exit on errors.
Default ruleset (162 rule IDs, lines 15-176); rule definitions live in ../rules/*.yml (84 files, 183 rules); sibling rulesets np.assets.yml (15) and np.hashes.yml (6).
Release build script used by CI and both Dockerfiles: cargo build --locked --features release, then assembles bin/, completions, man pages, JSON schema.

code.architecture: Cargo workspace of 8 crates (Cargo.toml:1-2). crates/noseyparker-cli is the binary: clap command definitions (src/args.rs), one module per command (cmd_scan.rs, cmd_report.rs + cmd_report/{human_format,sarif_format}.rs, cmd_summarize.rs, cmd_rules/, cmd_github.rs, cmd_datastore.rs, cmd_annotations.rs, cmd_generate/), and rule loading (rule_loader.rs). crates/noseyparker is the core library: SQLite datastore (src/datastore.rs + datastore/schema_70.sql, rusqlite bundled), a Vectorscan multi-pattern prefilter followed by anchored Rust-regex capture extraction (src/rules_database.rs, src/matcher.rs), blob/provenance/snippet types, git_binary.rs (shells out to the system git for clone/update with global/system config disabled), an optional github/ REST client (feature `github`, reqwest+tokio), and embedded default rules and ignore file via include_dir (src/defaults.rs, data/default/). crates/noseyparker-rules parses YAML rules/rulesets (rule fields: name, id, pattern, description, examples, negative_examples, references, categories; no validation/verification field, src/rule.rs:10-40). crates/input-enumerator walks the filesystem with the `ignore` crate but with standard filters disabled, so .gitignore and hidden files are not honored (src/lib.rs:224), and enumerates Git repos in-process via gix, iterating every object in the object database and computing first-seen commit/path provenance (src/git_repo_enumerator.rs, src/git_metadata_graph.rs). Smaller crates: noseyparker-digest (git-style SHA-1 blob ids), content-guesser (MIME guess, optional libmagic), bstring-serde, progress. Scan flow: rules compiled once -> enumerator thread feeds a bounded channel -> Rayon parallel scanner threads -> one datastore-writer thread committing batched SQLite transactions (cmd_scan.rs:403-447, 506-542). A datastore is a directory with datastore.db, scratch/, clones/, blobs/ and an auto-written .gitignore containing `*` (datastore.rs:107-133); concurrent multi-process use of one datastore is documented as untested (datastore.rs:48-49). Default ignore patterns (lockfiles, vendored test dirs, /proc /sys /dev) live in crates/noseyparker/data/default/ignore.conf.
code.packaging_and_release: Version 0.24.0 (Cargo.toml:15); every crate has `publish = false`, so nothing is published to crates.io. Release profile: opt-level 3, thin LTO, debuginfo stripped into packed split debuginfo (Cargo.toml:20-28); the `release` feature enables mimalloc and compiles out trace logging (crates/noseyparker-cli/Cargo.toml:59). scripts/create-release.zsh runs `cargo build --locked --profile release --features release` (line 112), copies target/release/noseyparker-cli to release/bin/noseyparker (119), adds CHANGELOG/LICENSE/README, .dwp/.dSYM debug symbols, completions for 5 shells, man pages and the report JSON schema (122-152), and prints per-file sha256 digests to the build log only (157-158). .github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml (push to main, tags v*.*.*, manual) builds ubuntu-22.04 x86_64/arm64 and macos-13 x86_64/arm64 natively plus Alpine/musl amd64/arm64 via Dockerfile.alpine, runs the integration tests against the built binary, and uploads noseyparker-v<ver>-<target-triple>.tar.gz as GitHub Actions artifacts (release-artifacts.yml:15-157); no step creates a GitHub Release or emits checksum, signature or attestation files. .github/workflows/docker-image.yml builds Debian- and Alpine-based images per arch on native runners, pushes by digest to ghcr.io/<repo>[-alpine] and merges multi-arch manifests (docker-image.yml:32-174); no signing/attestation step. macOS codesign + notarization (Developer ID identity, notarytool) exists only as a manual script (scripts/codesign-macos-release.zsh:38-39, 66, 77) not invoked by any workflow. Homebrew and AUR packages are third-party (README.md:260-261). Vectorscan can optionally be built CPU-native, which breaks binary portability (crates/noseyparker-cli/Cargo.toml:34-43).
code.tests_and_ci: Rust `cargo test`: unit tests in several crates plus CLI integration tests in crates/noseyparker-cli/tests/ (16 .rs files, 195 insta .snap snapshot files) using assert_cmd, assert_fs, insta, predicates; about 131 matching test-attribute lines in 25 files (about 90 in the integration tests, about 41 in crate sources). NP_TEST_PROGRAM lets the suite run against a built release binary or Docker image (tests/common/mod.rs:90-108). In-repo gaps: TODO list at tests/test_noseyparker.rs:20-36 (SARIF, --github-user/--github-org scans, datastore version mismatch, etc.); SARIF snapshot test is disabled (tests/scan/appmaker/mod.rs:54-57); Git-history scanning is exercised only by an empty-repo test and a network clone of an archived third-party repo (tests/scan/basic/mod.rs:117-127; tests/scan/appmaker/mod.rs:18-34), with no local multi-commit repo fixture; no tests in the progress or content-guesser crates and one in input-enumerator. CI workflows: ci.yml (PR, push to main, daily 05:00 UTC cron) runs a 7-job matrix (ubuntu-22.04 x86_64 release+test, ubuntu-24.04 x86_64 --no-default-features, ubuntu-22.04 arm64 release, ubuntu-24.04 arm64 test, macos-13 x86_64, macos-14 arm64) with `cargo test --locked` (NP_GITHUB_TOKEN from secrets so GitHub tests hit the live API), `--version`, and `cargo doc` under -D warnings (ci.yml:50-186); rust-checks.yml (PR/push/tags + weekly cron) runs clippy -> SARIF -> GitHub code scanning with continue-on-error (non-blocking) and `cargo fmt --all --check` (rust-checks.yml:13-93); release-artifacts.yml and docker-image.yml as described above (the Docker job smoke-tests `--version`, docker-image.yml:107-108). No MSRV job: CI uses stable (Cargo.toml:7 declares rust-version 1.82; Dockerfile:12 builds with rust:1.82-bullseye).
code.dependencies: Cargo workspace; Cargo.lock is committed and CI/release build with --locked (ci.yml:168-180; scripts/create-release.zsh:112). MSRV 1.82 (Cargo.toml:7). Direct dependency entries per manifest (workspace path crates included): crates/noseyparker-cli/Cargo.toml 45 runtime (6 optional; 6 are workspace crates) + 6 dev + 2 build (vergen, vergen-gitcl); crates/noseyparker/Cargo.toml 28 runtime (4 optional: chrono, reqwest, secrecy, tokio; 5 workspace crates) + 2 dev; crates/input-enumerator/Cargo.toml 14 + 1 dev; crates/noseyparker-rules/Cargo.toml 9 + 2 dev; crates/bstring-serde/Cargo.toml 4 + 2 dev; crates/content-guesser/Cargo.toml 4 (magic/libmagic optional); crates/noseyparker-digest/Cargo.toml 2 + 1 dev; crates/progress/Cargo.toml 1; the root Cargo.toml is a virtual workspace manifest with no dependencies. Notable: vectorscan-rs 0.0.5 (pre-1.0 C++ Vectorscan binding; needs cmake and Boost to build; Cargo.lock:4949-4963), rusqlite 0.35 with bundled SQLite, reqwest 0.12 with native-tls-vendored (vendored OpenSSL, Cargo.lock:3270-3271), gix 0.72.1 (Cargo.lock:1148-1149), parquet/arrow 55 (optional), serde_yaml 0.9.34+deprecated (Cargo.lock:4135-4136).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md exists: only the latest release receives security updates (SECURITY.md:5); vulnerabilities are reported by email to security@praetorian.com (SECURITY.md:9). The file has no private-vulnerability-reporting link, PGP key or response-time commitment.

claim_checks.claim: Natively scans files, directories, GitHub, and Git history (README.md:12).
claim_checks.evidence: `scan` accepts file/directory/local-repo inputs, --git-url, --github-user/--github-organization and --enumerator (crates/noseyparker-cli/src/args.rs:855-931); directories that are Git repos get their entire history scanned via object-database enumeration (crates/input-enumerator/src/git_repo_enumerator.rs:262-274; cmd_scan.rs:245-279). Code adds limits the README does not state: no staged-changes/diff mode, and --git-history only accepts full|none, with a code comment noting bounded history is unimplemented (args.rs:776-783).

claim_checks.claim: Uses regular expressions with 183 patterns chosen for high precision (README.md:13).
claim_checks.evidence: The count is right: 183 rule definitions in 84 YAML files (crates/noseyparker/data/default/builtin/rules/; 183 top-level `- name:` entries and 183 `  id:` lines), matching 162 (rulesets/default.yml:15-176) + 15 (np.assets.yml:14-29, one commented out at :22) + 6 (np.hashes.yml:13-18). But a default scan enables only the `default` ruleset (args.rs:724), i.e., 162 rules; the other 21 are asset/identifier and password-hash rules. 'High precision' is not checkable; the default set includes 14 generic rules (default.yml:56-69) and fuzzy-category rules need surrounding context (docs/RULES.md:90).

claim_checks.claim: Deduplicates matches that share the same secret, reducing review burden by 10-1000x or more (README.md:14).
claim_checks.evidence: Mechanism verified: a finding is the group of matches sharing a rule and capture groups (crates/noseyparker/src/datastore/schema_70.sql:159-186; README.md:131-134) and redundant-match suppression is on by default in `report` (args.rs:1105-1110). The 10-1000x magnitude is self-reported with no method or dataset.

claim_checks.claim: Can scan at GB/s on a multicore system and has scanned inputs as large as 20TB (README.md:15; example at README.md:158-160).
claim_checks.evidence: No benchmark harness in the repo (criterion commented out at crates/noseyparker-cli/Cargo.toml:120; FIXME 'add benchmarks' at crates/noseyparker/src/location.rs:114) and the README example gives no hardware. The design is consistent with a throughput focus (Vectorscan multi-pattern prefilter, matcher.rs:132-153; Rayon parallel scanners, cmd_scan.rs:327-331, 506-542).

claim_checks.claim: Prebuilt binaries for x86_64/aarch64 Linux and macOS are on the latest release page (README.md:34).
claim_checks.evidence: .github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml builds tarballs for ubuntu-22.04 x86_64/arm64 and macos-13 x86_64/arm64 (lines 22-44) and Alpine/musl amd64/arm64 (91-103), but only uploads them as Actions workflow artifacts (80-86, 151-157). No workflow publishes GitHub Release assets, checksums, signatures or attestations, so the Releases-page contents cannot be verified from this repo.

claim_checks.claim: Docker images for x86_64/aarch64 at ghcr.io/praetorian-inc/noseyparker and -alpine, with :latest and :main tags (README.md:37-51).
claim_checks.evidence: .github/workflows/docker-image.yml:36-62 builds Debian and Alpine images for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 on native runners and :125-174 merges them into multi-arch manifests (triggers: push to main and v*.*.* tags, :15-20). Entrypoint `noseyparker` with /scan workdir matches the README usage (Dockerfile:66-68; Dockerfile.alpine:40-42). No image signing or attestation step.

claim_checks.claim: Additional output formats are supported, including JSON and JSON lines (README.md:226).
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the README: `report` supports human, json, jsonl and sarif (args.rs:1287-1309). SARIF is not mentioned in the README, is labelled experimental (args.rs:1301-1307; CHANGELOG.md:323), has its tests disabled/TODO (crates/noseyparker-cli/tests/scan/appmaker/mod.rs:54-57; tests/test_noseyparker.rs:27), lists only built-in rules (cmd_report/sarif_format.rs:154-156), and embeds the matching text in snippet.text (sarif_format.rs:88-92).

claim_checks.claim: Man pages converted to Markdown are included in the repository at docs/v0.17.0/man/man1 (README.md:98-99).
claim_checks.evidence: The files exist but are for v0.17.0 while the workspace version is 0.24.0 (Cargo.toml:15). The v0.17.0 `report` page predates --min-score, --max-provenance and --suppress-redundant (args.rs:1070-1110) and the `scan` page predates --enumerator (args.rs:894-912); grep of docs/v0.17.0 finds none of these. The release tarball generates fresh man pages (scripts/create-release.zsh:146).

claim_checks.claim: Nosey Parker also includes vendored copies of several other packages under the Apache License and other permissive licenses; see LICENSE for details (README.md:292).
claim_checks.evidence: LICENSE (lines 1-202) is only the stock Apache-2.0 text with no list of vendored packages, there is no NOTICE or third-party license file, and the tree has no vendored-package directories. CHANGELOG.md:317-321 and 330 say the vendored Boost/Vectorscan copies were removed from this repo and moved into the separate vectorscan-rs crates.

claim_checks.claim: The project has pre-commit hooks that readers are encouraged to use (README.md:278-283).
claim_checks.evidence: .pre-commit-config.yaml:3-23 configures contributor hygiene hooks (check-added-large-files, check-yaml/json/toml, check-symlinks, trailing-whitespace, rustfmt `fmt`, `cargo-check`). None runs Nosey Parker or any secret scanner, and no .pre-commit-hooks.yaml is published for downstream use (glob finds none), so the README line concerns repo contributors, not scanning staged changes.

risks: No staged-changes/pre-commit mode: inputs are paths, local repos, HTTPS URLs, GitHub users/orgs or JSONL enumerator files (crates/noseyparker-cli/src/args.rs:855-931); local Git scanning iterates every blob in the object database (crates/input-enumerator/src/git_repo_enumerator.rs:143-163, 262-274; git_metadata_graph.rs:185-226) and --git-history accepts only full|none (args.rs:776-783). No .pre-commit-hooks.yaml is shipped and the seen-blob set is per run (cmd_scan.rs:472), so a per-commit hook would rescan the whole repo each time. Inference, untested: blobs written by `git add` are loose objects and would be enumerated, but no code, doc or test targets staged content.

CI gating and coverage gaps: exit status is 0 whether or not findings exist (main.rs:124-136 only exits 2 on error; tests/scan/basic/mod.rs:130-135 asserts success with 1 match), and enumeration/read errors are logged while the scan still succeeds (cmd_scan.rs:509-541; tests/scan/basic/mod.rs:99-115), so CI must parse `report -f json|jsonl|sarif` or `summarize -f json`. Silent-by-default skips: files over --max-file-size (default 100 MB) get only a debug-level message (crates/input-enumerator/src/lib.rs:138-139; args.rs:988-998), symlinks are not followed (lib.rs:158-162, 222), and default path ignores cover lockfiles, vendored test dirs and /proc /sys /dev (crates/noseyparker/data/default/ignore.conf:34-38, 60-63), also applied to Git-history paths (CHANGELOG.md:267-268).

No credential verification: rules are regex-only (crates/noseyparker-rules/src/rule.rs:10-40; crates/noseyparker/src/matcher.rs:143-155) and the only HTTP client enumerates GitHub repos (crates/noseyparker/src/github/client.rs:35-68), so findings are never classified live/revoked. The default ruleset includes 14 generic rules (rulesets/default.yml:56-69). There is no inline allowlist or baseline mechanism (grep finds none); triage state is accept/reject annotations inside the datastore (args.rs:1113-1125).

Findings and token handling: the datastore keeps the matching text plus about 256 bytes of context per match in plaintext SQLite (crates/noseyparker/src/datastore/schema_70.sql:142-154, 215-222; args.rs:667-677), --copy-blobs can copy whole blobs (args.rs:679-693), JSON/SARIF reports embed matches (cmd_report/sarif_format.rs:88-92), and no redaction option exists (grep). The default datastore path is `datastore.np` in the current directory (args.rs:78); it self-writes a .gitignore of `*` (datastore.rs:107-110) and is skipped by later scans (input-enumerator/src/lib.rs:145-152), but the README does not discuss handling these artifacts. Separately, NP_GITHUB_TOKEN is passed to git via an always-on credential helper (git_binary.rs:30-36) and --git-url accepts any HTTPS host (git_url.rs:59-61), so it may be offered to non-GitHub hosts (inference from code, untested).

Stability and maintenance: version 0.24.0 is pre-1.0 and semver is claimed only for the CLI and output formats (Cargo.toml:15; CHANGELOG.md:6-7), yet v0.22.0 broke the JSON output and datastore schema (CHANGELOG.md:62-77). Datastores from other versions are rejected with no migration (crates/noseyparker/src/datastore.rs:1053-1063, 1081-1088). SARIF is experimental and untested (args.rs:1301-1307; tests/test_noseyparker.rs:27). The latest CHANGELOG entry is v0.24.0 dated 2025-05-08 (CHANGELOG.md:10); this shallow checkout pinned at the tag cannot show later activity. One author is listed (Cargo.toml:10) and the regex-engine binding vectorscan-rs 0.0.5 lives in a separate personal-account repo (CHANGELOG.md:330; Cargo.lock:4949-4950).

Release and supply-chain hygiene: workflows only upload Actions artifacts and push GHCR images, with no checksum files, signatures or attestations (.github/workflows/release-artifacts.yml:73-86, 151-157; docker-image.yml:87-174); macOS signing/notarization is a manual script not wired to CI (scripts/codesign-macos-release.zsh:38-39, 66, 77). Third-party actions use mutable refs such as @master, @v2, @v4 (ci.yml:144-161; release-artifacts.yml:47-58). No dependabot, cargo-deny or cargo-audit config found; the lockfile contains serde_yaml 0.9.34+deprecated (Cargo.lock:4135-4136); clippy is non-blocking (rust-checks.yml:60-65). Docker bases are Debian 11 pinned (Dockerfile:12, 56) and floating alpine:latest / rust:alpine (Dockerfile.alpine:6, 33), and images run as root (no USER directive).

Platform and build constraints: no native Windows (README.md:61-62) and WSL2 is undocumented; building needs cmake, Boost >=1.57, zsh, patch, pkg-config and a C++ toolchain via vectorscan-rs-sys (README.md:72-80). CI and release cover only Ubuntu and macOS on pinned runner labels (ubuntu-22.04/24.04, macos-13/14: ci.yml:59-141; release-artifacts.yml:22-44), and the changelog records a forced runner bump when GitHub removed ubuntu-20.04 (CHANGELOG.md:41). Several integration tests need live GitHub access (crates/noseyparker-cli/tests/github/mod.rs; tests/scan/appmaker/mod.rs:18-34; ci.yml:173-180).

Licensing documentation mismatch: README.md:292 says LICENSE details vendored third-party packages, but LICENSE is only the Apache-2.0 text (LICENSE:1-202) and the repo has no NOTICE or third-party license file, while builds bundle third-party C/C++ code: SQLite (rusqlite `bundled`, crates/noseyparker/Cargo.toml:46), OpenSSL (`native-tls-vendored`, Cargo.toml:45; Cargo.lock:3270-3271) and Vectorscan (vectorscan-rs-sys, Cargo.lock:4962-4963). Those components' licenses are not visible in this checkout.
